subject: Senior call recap — operational goals, procurement map and SLA considerations
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@novaplex.com>, Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@novaplex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 May 2028 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Senior call recap — operational goals, procurement map and SLA considerations

Thanks again for the conversation today, Sarah and Carlos — appreciate the candid overview of the production constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we loop Procurement and Legal.

Key pain points (as discussed)
- Intermittent p95 latency spikes during evening batch loads (current peak p95 ~480ms)
- Unpredictable unit cost when model usage spikes — finance needs a stable forecast for next quarter
- Data segregation & audit log retention requirements for regulated data (7+ years)
- Need for an SLA that includes DR recovery windows and an ops escalation path to your 24/7 team

Primary goals
1) Pilot with clear SLOs: reduce p95 to <200ms for the targeted inference flow; maintain 99.9% availability for the pilot window
2) Produce an estimated TCO for 6-month pilot and a forecast for steady-state — finance wants a conservative and an aggressive scenario
3) Compliance evidence: SOC 2 summary, KMS/HSM support, and audit log details to support your security review

Procurement path (proposed)
- Week 0–2: POC planning + environment setup (dedicated pool for predictable throughput)
- Week 3–6: Pilot execution (joint acceptance criteria)
- Weeks 7–10: Legal & procurement review of commercial/SLA terms; target for enterprise contract 

Immediate next steps
- Attached: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan), SOC2_Summary.pdf, Draft_SLA_Addendum.docx
- Sarah/Carlos: please confirm procurement contact and preferred kickoff window (proposed: Thu 5/11 or Mon 5/15)
- Hannah/Marissa/Sean: we will prepare the TCO scenarios and a lightweight architecture diagram for the procurement kickoff

If I missed anything important from today, flag below — otherwise I’ll schedule the kickoff once you confirm the procurement owner and an available slot.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@novaplex.com>

Cc: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@novaplex.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procure@novaplex.com>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Senior call recap — operational goals, procurement map and SLA considerations

Thanks, Hannah — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side and an ask so we can pull the right stakeholders in: 

1) Procurement lead: Carlos will be the primary procurement contact; I’ve looped Procurement (procure@novaplex.com) for scheduling. Legal lead is Emily R. (cc will follow after we set the internal kickoff).
2) Timeline constraints: Legal will likely need ~3 weeks for redlines; Security will need ~4 weeks for compliance testing (we’d like the SOC2/KMS detail up front). Our target is to get commercial approval in Q3 budget cycle, so speed matters.
3) SLA exceptions: we have an internal requirement for a DR recovery RTO/RPO clause that goes beyond standard templates. Can Redwood provide a proposed exception language for the Draft_SLA_Addendum? We need a clear ops escalation ladder (phone + pager) during business-critical hours.
4) TCO ask: can you surface both a pilot-only TCO (6 months) and a projected annual steady-state TCO, including estimate line items for dedicated GPU pool vs. burst capacity? A short table would be ideal for our finance partner.

Quoting your section: 
> Procurement path (proposed)
> - Week 0–2: POC planning + environment setup (dedicated pool for predictable throughput)
> - Week 3–6: Pilot execution (joint acceptance criteria)
> - Weeks 7–10: Legal & procurement review of commercial/SLA terms; target for enterprise contract

That matches our internal thinking — thanks. We can do Thu 5/11 morning for an initial procurement alignment (Carlos and I available 09:00–11:30 PT). Please include the Procurement Team in the invite.

Sarah Bennett
VP, Platform Engineering | NovaPlex Health

Subject: Re: Senior call recap — operational goals, procurement map and SLA considerations

Looping in a few operational notes from a CS perspective — want to make sure we capture risk mitigations and an owner map for the kickoff.

Operational risk & mitigations
- Latency spikes: propose an early canary rollout focused on the 3 busiest endpoints + dedicated inference pool for the pilot to bound performance variance. Owner: Marissa (CS) + Engineering lead assigned during POC.
- Cost variance: we will model both dedicated pool and burst scenario in the TCO spreadsheet. Action: Hannah to share baseline usage shape (tokens/reqs per hour) so we can simulate costs.
- Compliance: Redwood can provide SOC 2 artifact summary and a KMS/HSM integration checklist. For long-term retention (7 years) we recommend a hybrid retention plan (short-term hot logs + archived cold storage) — Legal to advise on retention triggers.

Contract/SLA notes
- Draft_SLA_Addendum: I’ll draft suggested language for DR RTO/RPO exceptions and an ops escalation ladder (will mark as redline-friendly for your Legal team).
- Escalation: recommend capturing a named executive point-of-contact for 24/7 escalate-to in the MAP to reduce friction.

Next steps (internal owners)
- Hannah: confirm dates and invite Procurement (Carlos) to Thu 5/11 09:30 PT kickoff
- Marissa: produce a first-pass TCO scenarios and proposed DR language by EOD Mon 5/15
- Sean: send the pilot topology and preliminary capacity numbers to Sarah for review

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
